claims.text: The initial titanium- and nickel-containing high-entropy alloy is a single-phase solid solution produced by conventional casting.
Additive manufacturing will produce finer grains than conventional casting in this alloy.
Additive manufacturing will produce a more homogeneous microstructure than conventional casting in this alloy.
Rapid solidification during additive manufacturing will reduce chemical segregation.
Rapid solidification during additive manufacturing will promote more uniform nucleation.
Reduced segregation and more uniform nucleation will refine the alloy's grain structure.
The refined and more homogeneous microstructure will mitigate grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
The refined and more homogeneous microstructure will mitigate diffusion-related softening at elevated temperature.
Additively manufactured samples will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than conventionally cast samples of the same composition.
Additively manufactured samples will have lower elevated-temperature creep rates than conventionally cast samples of the same composition.
Additively manufactured samples will exhibit better overall elevated-temperature mechanical performance than conventionally cast samples.
The proposed effect applies above 600°C when oxidation or reactive degradation is minimized.
The magnitude of improvement may depend strongly on additive-manufacturing parameters.
The magnitude of improvement may depend strongly on post-processing heat treatment needed to stabilize the refined microstructure.
